artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent authoritative master-system contact-point identifier; where the adopting Dimension publishes contact data as linked data, a governed IRI may additionally be minted, but the URI value itself is never the record identifier because handles are transferable.

findings.name: Postal delivery endpoint reference and delivery role
findings.description: A contact point may designate a postal delivery endpoint. UPU S42 Part A defines the postal address component set and Part B the country-specific templates that render components into a correctly formatted address; that structure, its maintenance and any geocoding belong to the postal-address and place models. This model carries the reference to the addressed location, the country binding that selects the template, and the delivery-role attributes that are properties of the contact arrangement rather than of the location: attention line, care-of, and mailbox or post-office-box designation.

questions.text: Which addressed location does this postal contact point designate, and by which reference is that location identified?
answer_data: Full address text captured at time of reference

questions.text: Which country template and postal component set govern rendition of this address for delivery?
Which delivery-specific attributes belong to the contact point rather than to the location itself?
Is the delivery point a place the party occupies, or purely a mail-receipt arrangement such as a box or forwarding agent?

data_elements.name: Addressed location reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the address or place record held by the postal-address/place model.

data_elements.name: Postal country code
data_elements.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code selecting the applicable country template, as required by JSContact Address countryCode.

data_elements.name: Attention line
data_elements.description: Recipient-routing line naming the person or unit to whose attention items are delivered.

data_elements.name: Care-of party
data_elements.description: Party through whom delivery is routed when the recipient is not the occupant of the addressed location.

data_elements.name: Delivery service designation
data_elements.description: Post-office box, private bag, poste restante or comparable delivery-service designation attached to the contact arrangement.

data_elements.name: Captured full address text
data_elements.description: Free-text rendering of the address as supplied, retained only as provenance for the reference and never as the authoritative component structure.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The structured postal address components, the country template library and the rendition rules are defined and maintained under UPU S42 Parts A and B and materialized by the postal-address and place models. Producing a local address artifact here would duplicate a target-owned structure, desynchronize from the template library and create a second address of record; this model therefore holds only reference and delivery-role fields inline.

layers.name: Internationalization of endpoint values
layers.description: Script, encoding, normalization and localization rules that cut across all endpoint kinds.

findings.name: Script, normalization and localized forms
findings.description: Endpoint values and their labels must survive non-ASCII scripts. IDNA2008 requires U-labels to be in Normalization Form C and A-labels and U-labels to be mutually convertible; RFC 6530 permits UTF-8 throughout a mailbox; RFC 6068 defines percent-encoded UTF-8 for URI carriage. JSContact separates a card-level language tag from a localizations map that applies locale-specific overrides by JSON Pointer rather than duplicating the object. UPU reports at least twenty scripts in official postal use, so transliteration authority must be recorded rather than assumed.

questions.text: Which Unicode normalization form is required before an endpoint value is stored or compared?
Which language tag applies to the human-readable label for this endpoint?
answer_data: Default language of the containing profile

questions.text: How are localized alternative forms of one endpoint recorded without creating duplicate contact points?
answer_data: Localization variant set keyed by locale
Pointer or key linking each variant to the base value
Cardinality rule stating variants do not multiply the contact point

questions.text: Which script or transliteration variant is authoritative when a source system supplies more than one?

data_elements.name: Unicode normalization form
data_elements.description: Code stating the Unicode normalization form applied to the stored value; Normalization Form C where IDNA U-labels are involved.

data_elements.name: Endpoint label
data_elements.description: Human-readable label describing the endpoint, distinct from the endpoint value itself.

data_elements.name: Label language tag
data_elements.description: Language tag identifying the language of the label and of the localized variant.

data_elements.name: Localization variant
data_elements.description: Locale-keyed override of one or more fields of the endpoint, applied without duplicating the contact point.

data_elements.name: Transliteration authority
data_elements.description: Reference to the standard, authority or source system that produced a script variant of the value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Internationalization manifests as constraints and parallel value forms on the telephone, mailbox and URI endpoint artifacts already declared. Materializing localized variants as separate artifacts would fragment one endpoint across multiple records, break the A-label/U-label equivalence guarantee and inflate contact-point counts for what is a single reachable channel.

bundles.name: Endpoint assurance, validity and supersession
bundles.description: The evidence and time dimensions of a contact point: what was proven about control of the endpoint, when the endpoint is valid, whether it is currently reachable, and which contact point replaces it.
bundles.rationale: OpenID Connect models verified state as a provider assertion rather than an intrinsic property; NIST SP 800-63A places proofing procedure and assurance levels in a separate discipline; CPOV models contact availability as a temporal entity. Together these establish that assurance, validity and reachability are carried on the contact point but sourced and executed elsewhere.

layers.name: Verification assertions
layers.description: Assertions of proof of control over an endpoint, carried on the contact point without importing the proofing process.

findings.name: Carried verification assertion for endpoint control
findings.description: A contact point may carry the outcome of a proof-of-control check: which authority asserted it, which method class was used, which assurance level is claimed, when it was asserted, and when it expires. OpenID Connect defines email_verified and phone_number_verified as claims asserted by an issuing provider, which makes the asserting party a required part of the record. NIST SP 800-63A owns proofing and enrollment procedure and its assurance framing; this model therefore records the assertion and a reference to its evidence, and never the challenge issuance, evaluation logic, decision engine or proofing audit trail.

questions.text: Which authority asserted that the owning party controls this endpoint, and at what instant was the assertion made?
answer_data: Assertion subject binding to the contact-point identifier

questions.text: Which verification method class and assurance level does the assertion claim?
answer_data: Assurance level code and framework reference
Evidence reference held by the proofing model

questions.text: Does the assertion expire, and which events invalidate it before its stated expiry?
answer_data: Invalidating event codes such as endpoint value change or supersession

questions.text: Which system executed the proofing challenge, and where is the audit record of that execution held?
answer_data: Audit record locator held by the referenced model
Explicit statement that this model stores no execution or audit detail

data_elements.name: Verification assertion identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the assertion as issued by the asserting authority.

data_elements.name: Asserting authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the provider, steward or proofing service that made the verification assertion.

data_elements.name: Verification status
data_elements.description: Coded verified state of the endpoint, corresponding to claims such as email_verified or phone_number_verified.

data_elements.name: Verification method class
data_elements.description: Coded class of the proof-of-control method, recorded without the parameters or transcript of the run.

data_elements.name: Claimed assurance level
data_elements.description: Assurance level claimed by the assertion together with the framework that defines it.

data_elements.name: Assertion instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the asserting authority made the assertion (event time).

data_elements.name: Assertion recorded at
data_elements.description: Instant at which this model ingested the assertion (observation time), recorded separately from the assertion instant.

data_elements.name: Assertion expiry
data_elements.description: Instant after which the assertion is no longer treated as current.

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Opaque locator for the evidence held by the proofing or verification model; this model stores the locator only.

artifacts.name: Channel verification assertion
artifacts.description: A carried, self-contained assertion binding a contact-point identifier to a claim of proven control, with asserting authority, method class, assurance level, event and observation timestamps, expiry and an evidence locator. It is an inbound record, never a log of this model's own processing.
media_or_form: Assertion record in any encoding
Verified-claim payload such as an OpenID Connect email_verified or phone_number_verified claim
Signed attestation with a dereferenceable evidence locator
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the assertion identifier issued by the asserting authority as the authoritative master-system identifier; where an authority issues none, mint a governed IRI or, failing that, a UUID or ULID in the adopting Dimension and record the authority reference alongside it. The assertion instant is never used as the identifier.

layers.name: Validity, reachability and supersession
layers.description: Time-bounded validity of the contact point, its derived operational reachability status, and the ordered replacement chain that links retired contact points to their successors.

findings.name: Validity interval and lifecycle state
findings.description: A contact point is valid over an interval and holds a lifecycle state. CPOV models contact availability and availability restriction as temporal entities; JSContact and vCard carry only created/updated and REV, so a normative valid-from/valid-to on a contact point is not supplied by the cited contact standards and is declared here as an adopting-Dimension extension rather than as a standards claim. Open-ended intervals, scheduled future changes and asserted past end dates must be distinguishable.

questions.text: From which instant until which instant is this contact point valid for use by the owning party?
Which lifecycle state does the contact point currently hold, and which state transitions are permitted from it?
Is a recorded end date an assertion of past fact or a scheduled future change, and how is a still-open interval represented?
Are there recurring windows within the validity interval during which the contact point is available or restricted?

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: Instant from which the contact point is valid for use (event time).

data_elements.name: Valid to
data_elements.description: Instant after which the contact point ceases to be valid; absent means the interval is open-ended.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Coded state of the contact point such as proposed, active, suspended, superseded or retired.

data_elements.name: End-date nature
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing an asserted past end from a scheduled future change.

data_elements.name: Availability window
data_elements.description: Recurring window during which the contact point is normally available, aligned to CPOV opening hours.

data_elements.name: Availability restriction
data_elements.description: Interval or recurrence during which the contact point is explicitly not available.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is expressed as two instants, a state code and optional recurrence expressions carried directly on the contact-point record; it has no independent serialization and no consumer that needs it apart from the record it qualifies. It is recorded inline precisely because no cited contact standard defines it as a separate object, so inventing an artifact would present an unsupported structure as canonical.

findings.name: Operational reachability status
findings.description: A derived, time-stamped statement of whether the endpoint currently appears reachable, together with a locator for the evidence that supports it. The underlying transmission, delivery status, failure reports and engagement records are owned by the communication/message model under SMTP and comparable transport specifications; this model carries only the summarized status, its observation instant and the evidence reference. Reachability is deliberately separated from validity: an endpoint may be valid but temporarily unreachable, or reachable but no longer valid for the party.

questions.text: What is the last recorded reachability status of this endpoint and at which instant was it observed?
Which evidence supports the recorded reachability status, and in which model is that evidence held?
answer_data: Explicit statement that no attempt log is stored locally

questions.text: Does an unreachable status invalidate the contact point, or only suppress its operational use?
Who may set or override reachability status, and may it be set without an underlying observation?

data_elements.name: Reachability status
data_elements.description: Coded operational status such as reachable, degraded, unreachable-transient, unreachable-permanent or unknown.

data_elements.name: Reachability observed at
data_elements.description: Observation instant for the recorded status, distinct from the instant the status was ingested or from any endpoint event time.

data_elements.name: Reachability evidence reference
data_elements.description: Locator for the delivery or probe evidence held by the communication/message model; never the evidence itself.

data_elements.name: Reachability status setter
data_elements.description: Reference to the system or role that set the current status, including manual overrides.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Reachability is a derived summary field plus an evidence locator on the contact-point record. Declaring an artifact here would create a local observation store and would drift toward owning delivery-attempt, bounce and audit-trail semantics that belong to the referenced communication/message model; keeping it inline enforces that boundary structurally.

findings.name: Supersession and replacement chain
findings.description: When a party changes an endpoint, the old contact point is superseded rather than overwritten, so that verification assertions, historical references and inbound links remain interpretable. Supersession is an ordered, acyclic chain with an effective instant per link. No cited contact standard defines supersession for contact points - vCard offers only REV and JSContact only created/updated - so this is declared as an adopting-Dimension extension built on the identity separation those standards do provide.

questions.text: Which contact point replaces this one, and from which effective instant does the replacement apply?
Is a superseded contact point retained for historical interpretation, or disposed once the successor is active?
How is a supersession chain traversed to obtain the currently effective endpoint for a historical reference?
answer_data: Resolution outcome when the chain ends in a retired node

questions.text: What prevents a supersession cycle or a fork with two concurrent successors?

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a contact point to the contact point it replaces.

data_elements.name: Superseded-by reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a retired contact point to its active successor.

data_elements.name: Supersession effective instant
data_elements.description: Event-time instant from which the successor is the effective contact point.

data_elements.name: Supersession reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason for replacement such as party-initiated change, carrier reassignment, employer change or correction of an error.

data_elements.name: Supersession sequence number
data_elements.description: Monotonically increasing integer ordering supersession links within one contact-point chain.

artifacts.name: Supersession link entry
artifacts.description: An ordered entry recording that one contact point replaces another from a stated effective instant, with a reason code and sequence number, forming an acyclic chain per contact point.
media_or_form: Ordered replacement link record
Change-history entry in a party contact register
Directed edge in a contact-point graph projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the predecessor's authoritative master-system contact-point identifier combined with the chain sequence number; where the adopting Dimension issues no master-system key, a governed IRI or a UUID/ULID is minted. The effective instant is never part of the identifier.

functions.name: Register contact point
functions.description: Create a new contact point for an owning party, capturing the typed endpoint value, its declared kind, purpose contexts, capability features and initial validity, and assigning a stable identifier per the model identity priority.
outputs: Contact point record with assigned identifier
Normalized endpoint value and comparison key
Validation outcome with any rejected components
preconditions: Owning party reference resolves in the party model
Endpoint kind is present in the authoritative code list or carries a governed extension namespace
Registering actor is an authorized steward or the party itself
effects: A contact point record exists in lifecycle state proposed or active with an open validity interval
No verification status is asserted; verification_status remains absent until an assertion is attached
No permission to contact is created or implied; consent remains with the referenced consent model

functions.name: Normalize endpoint value
functions.description: Apply the scheme-specific canonicalization required for storage and comparison: E.164 digit form with visual separators removed for telephone numbers, case-preserving local-part handling with case-insensitive domain for mailboxes, the RFC 3986 comparison ladder for URIs, and Normalization Form C with A-label/U-label pairing for internationalized names.
inputs: Phone-context where the number is local
outputs: Display form where a notation standard applies
Normalization report listing each rule applied
preconditions: Endpoint kind and its governing specification are known
For a local telephone number, a phone-context is supplied
Input encoding is declared or reliably detected as UTF-8
effects: Canonical and display forms are stored as parallel representations of one endpoint, never as separate contact points
Mailbox local-part case is preserved verbatim and is never folded
Values that fail scheme validation are rejected with a reason rather than silently coerced

functions.name: Attach channel verification assertion
functions.description: Record an externally produced proof-of-control assertion against a contact point, capturing the asserting authority, method class, claimed assurance level, event and observation instants, expiry and evidence locator. This function records an outcome; it never issues challenges, evaluates responses or determines assurance.
inputs: Assertion identifier and asserting authority reference
Method class and assurance level codes
outputs: Channel verification assertion linked to the contact point
Updated verification status on the contact point
Rejection report where the assertion subject does not match the contact point
preconditions: Contact point exists and is not retired
Asserting authority is recognized by the adopting Dimension
Assertion subject binding matches the contact-point identifier and current endpoint value
effects: The contact point carries a verification assertion with separate event and observation timestamps
No proofing challenge is issued and no evaluation is performed by this model
The proofing execution record and its audit trail remain in the referenced identity-proofing model and are not copied here

functions.name: Resolve contact point to current endpoint
functions.description: Dereference a contact-point identifier or a historical endpoint value to the currently effective contact point by following the supersession chain, returning the canonical endpoint value, validity state and verification status without applying any preference ranking.
inputs: Contact point identifier or normalized comparison key
outputs: Canonical endpoint value and display form
Validity state and verification status at the resolution instant
preconditions: Supersession chain is acyclic and has at most one active successor per node
Requesting actor holds read access to the contact point
effects: A resolution result is returned as of the supplied instant; no record is mutated
Where the chain terminates in a retired node with no successor, an explicit unresolved outcome is returned rather than a stale value
Preference ranking and channel selection are not performed here; they belong to the preferences layer of this model

functions.name: Supersede contact point
functions.description: Close the validity interval of a contact point, move it to the superseded state and create an ordered supersession link to a successor contact point with an effective instant and reason code.
outputs: Supersession link entry with sequence number
Updated predecessor state and closed validity interval
Updated successor with a supersedes reference
preconditions: Both contact points exist and belong to the same owning party
The successor is not already superseding another active node in a way that would create a cycle or a second concurrent successor
The acting steward is authorized for the owning party
effects: The predecessor is retained under the applicable retention rule and is not deleted by this function
Verification assertions attached to the predecessor are marked invalidated by supersession but are not transferred to the successor
Downstream disposition of the retained predecessor is decided by the adopting Dimension's retention policy, not by this function

composition.purpose: WM-PER-010 is mixed into the party model to supply the contact profile. It carries only a reference to the owning party plus the party-kind facet needed to select validation rules; party identifiers, names, matching and party lifecycle stay in the target.

composition.target: Postal address / place model (registry identifier unresolved)
composition.purpose: The postal endpoint carries a reference to an addressed location plus the delivery-role parameters (attention line, care-of, box designation) and the country code that selects a template. Address component structure, template rendition, geocoding and address lifecycle remain owned by the target.

composition.target: Communication event / message-delivery model (registry identifier unresolved)
composition.purpose: Reachability status carries a locator for delivery or probe evidence held by the target. Message content, envelopes, delivery attempts, failure reports and engagement records are not modelled here.

composition.target: Identity proofing and verification-process model (registry identifier unresolved)
composition.purpose: Verification assertions carry the asserting authority, method class, assurance level, timestamps and an evidence locator. Challenge issuance, evaluation, assurance determination and the proofing audit trail remain wholly in the target.

composition.target: Consent and legal-basis model (registry identifier unresolved)
composition.purpose: Purpose contexts declared on an endpoint state intended use only. Permission to contact, lawful basis, withdrawal and objection outcomes are referenced from the target; neither JSContact nor schema.org ContactPoint carries consent semantics, so no local permission structure is created.

composition.target: ITU-T E.164 and IETF RFC 3966 tel URI
composition.purpose: Alignment for the canonical telephone endpoint: 15-digit maximum, CC/NDC/SN structure, global versus local numbers, mandatory phone-context and separator-insensitive comparison. Conformance is not claimed without validation evidence per instance.
Alignment for the human-readable display form of telephone numbers, email addresses and web addresses, held separately from the canonical machine form.

composition.target: IETF RFC 5321, RFC 6068, RFC 6530 and RFC 5890
composition.purpose: Alignment for mailbox syntax, case-sensitivity of local parts, mailto projection, internationalized email and IDNA A-label/U-label handling.
Alignment for URI component structure and the normalization/comparison ladder applied to web and online-service endpoints.

Primary interchange alignment: Card uid, Id-keyed channel maps, contexts, features, pref, label, countryCode, language and localizations map to this model's identity, classification and internationalization elements.

composition.target: IETF RFC 6350 vCard 4.0 and the W3C vCard Ontology
composition.purpose: Legacy and RDF alignment for TEL, EMAIL, ADR, URL and IMPP with TYPE, PREF, PID and ALTID, and for hasTelephone, hasEmail, hasAddress and hasURL in the RDF projection. The W3C document is an Interest Group Note, not a Recommendation.

Publication alignment for contactType, contactOption, areaServed, availableLanguage, hoursAvailable, email, telephone and faxNumber. schema.org aggregates several channels on one ContactPoint whereas this model holds one typed endpoint per contact point; the mapping is therefore one-to-many.

composition.target: UPU S42 international postal address components and templates
composition.purpose: Alignment for the postal component set (Part A) and country template library (Part B) that the referenced address model implements; this model aligns only its country binding and delivery-role attributes.

composition.target: SEMIC Core Public Organisation Vocabulary ContactPoint
composition.purpose: Public-sector alignment for contact point as a first-class class with email, telephone, contact page, opening hours and availability restriction expressed as temporal entities.

composition.target: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 verified contact claims
composition.purpose: Alignment for email_verified and phone_number_verified as provider-asserted claims, binding this model's verification status to an identifiable asserting authority.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable owner for the contact-profile package; per the registry this is the person themselves or an explicitly authorized identity steward, and that assignment is recorded as a resolvable reference, not as free text.
The owner package must declare its authoritative contact system of record, because the identity priority depends on a named master system issuing contact-point identifiers.

The owner package must bind to a postal-address/place model, a communication/message model, an identity-proofing model and a consent model before any contact point that references them is activated, or explicitly record the reference as unresolved.
The owner package must publish its retention schedule and disposition authority for contact records, since this model defines the tombstone shape but not the retention period.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers use the cp-chan- prefix within the WM-PER-010 namespace. External code values (endpoint kind, purpose context, capability feature, country code, language tag, URI scheme) are carried as namespaced references to their governing registry rather than copied into a local enumeration; adopting-Dimension extensions use a distinct extension namespace so that registered and local values are always distinguishable.
registry_links: IANA Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) Schemes registry for endpoint URI schemes
IANA vCard Elements registry for TYPE and property values
IANA JSContact registries for contexts, phone features and service names
ITU-T assigned country codes published in the ITU Operational Bulletin for E.164 country codes
UPU S42 Part B country template library for postal rendition
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for postal country codes and IETF BCP 47 for language tags

canonicalization_rules: Endpoint values are canonicalized by scheme, not generically: E.164 digit form with visual separators removed for telephone; case-preserved local part with lowercased domain for mailboxes; the RFC 3986 syntax-based level plus any declared scheme-based rule for URIs; Normalization Form C for all Unicode text.

The canonical form, the display form and any URI projection are stored as parallel representations of one endpoint and never as separate contact points; the applied normalization profile is recorded so that equivalence decisions are reproducible.
Comparison keys are derived, never authoritative: a canonical form may be recomputed when a normalization profile version changes, but the contact-point identifier must not change as a result.
patch_rules: A change to the endpoint value is a supersession, not an in-place update: the existing contact point is closed and a successor is created, so that verification assertions and historical references stay interpretable.

In-place patches are permitted only for non-identifying qualifiers - label, purpose context, capability feature, availability window, reachability status - and each patch records the actor, the event instant and the observation instant.
Localized variants are applied as locale-keyed overrides against a base value rather than as duplicate records, following the JSContact localizations pattern.
A patch that would set verification status without an accompanying assertion identifier and asserting authority reference is rejected.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new endpoint kind, purpose context or capability code is backward compatible; removing or re-meaning an existing code is breaking and requires a new package version plus a mapping table.
Consumers must tolerate absent optional elements; absence of verification status means unasserted, never unverified-as-fact, and absence of valid-to means an open interval, never expired.
Alignment mappings to vCard, JSContact, schema.org and CPOV are versioned against the cited specification version; a target specification revision does not silently change this model's semantics.

Because schema.org ContactPoint aggregates multiple channels on one node, export mappings must be declared one-to-many and round-trip loss must be documented rather than resolved by merging contact points.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the contact-point identifier issued by the named contact system of record for the owning party, or, for a verification assertion, the assertion identifier issued by the asserting authority.
Governed global identifier or IRI issued under a namespace the adopting Dimension controls or is delegated, used when no master-system identifier exists.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, and always recorded together with the minting system reference.

Endpoint values (E.164 number, addr-spec, URI, handle) are comparison keys only and are never identifiers, because carriers and services reassign them; a date or timestamp is never an identifier under any circumstance.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are expressed per RFC 3339 as date-time with explicit seconds and either the literal 'Z' or a numeric UTC offset; local wall-clock strings without an offset are rejected. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they differ: endpoint event times (valid-from, valid-to, supersession effective instant, verification assertion instant) are distinct elements from observation or ingestion times (record created/updated, verification recorded-at, reachability observed-at), and a consumer must never substitute one for the other.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - supersession link entries - are numbered per contact-point chain with a monotonically increasing, gap-free integer sequence starting at 1 and rendered as <contact_point_id>#<sequence>. Sequence numbers are never reused after a link is retracted and never encode a date, a year or any other temporal value.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each artifact carries a content digest (algorithm identifier plus digest value) computed over its canonical serialization together with the canonicalization profile version used. A stored artifact whose recomputed digest differs from the recorded digest is treated as corrupt, is served read-only with an integrity-failure flag, and must be re-attested by the owning steward before further use; verification assertions additionally retain any signature supplied by the asserting authority so that integrity can be checked without contacting that authority.

policies: Endpoint values are personal data by default and are minimized on read: consumers receive the narrowest form that satisfies the stated purpose, and a masked or partial form is served where a full value is not required.
Verification status may only be set from a recorded assertion naming an asserting authority; this model never self-asserts verification and never re-derives assurance levels.
Contact points are superseded rather than overwritten, and superseded records are retained under the adopting Dimension's schedule so that historical references and assertions stay interpretable.
Declaring a purpose context grants no permission to contact; every operational use must resolve permission against the referenced consent and legal-basis model.
Alignment to an external standard is recorded as a mapping with a version; conformance is asserted only where per-instance validation evidence exists.

read: Reads are scoped by owning party and by purpose: a consumer supplies a stated purpose and receives only the contact points whose purpose contexts and access classification admit it.
Full endpoint values, verification evidence locators and reachability evidence locators are separately gated from the contact-point metadata (identifier, kind, purpose, validity state).
Historical and superseded contact points are readable only through an explicit as-of resolution request that records the resolution instant.
create: Creation requires a resolvable owning-party reference, a declared endpoint kind, a raw value that passes scheme validation after normalization, and a recorded provenance for the value.
A newly created contact point starts with no verification status and no permission; both must be supplied by their owning models.
Creation is rejected where an active, non-superseded contact point for the same party already carries the same normalized comparison key, unless a duplicate-resolution outcome is recorded.
update: In-place update is limited to non-identifying qualifiers; any change to the endpoint value routes to the supersession function instead.
Every update records the acting identity, the event instant and the ingestion instant, and preserves the prior value in the record's change history.
Updating verification status, assurance level or asserting authority is permitted only as part of attaching or invalidating an assertion, never as a free-form field edit.
delete: Default disposition is soft: close the validity interval, set lifecycle state to retired and apply the adopting Dimension's retention schedule; hard deletion before schedule expiry requires a recorded authority reference and reason.

A retired or erased contact point leaves a tombstone containing only the contact-point identifier, the owning-party reference, the endpoint kind and the disposition instant, so that inbound references and supersession chains do not dangle; endpoint values, labels, display forms and evidence locators are purged from the tombstone.

This model does not own erasure execution, legal-hold evaluation or data-subject-request workflow. The adopting Dimension's retention and privacy policy decides the schedule; the referenced consent and legal-basis model decides whether an erasure obligation exists; the referenced audit model, not this model, holds the record of the erasure having been performed.

Verification assertions are disposed with the contact point they annotate unless the referenced identity-proofing model requires independent retention, in which case only this model's local copy of the assertion and its locator are removed and the proofing model's own copy is untouched.

roles.name: Contact data steward
responsibilities: Maintain contact points on behalf of the owning party within recorded authority
Resolve duplicate and conflicting contact points and record the outcome
Approve manual reachability overrides and record their justification

roles.name: Owning party (data subject or organization)
responsibilities: Supply and correct their own contact points and delivery-role attributes
Request supersession or disposition of a contact point
Receive notification when a contact point is added, verified or retired on their behalf

roles.name: Model maintainer / registrar
responsibilities: Version the model package, its alignment mappings and its canonicalization profiles
Maintain the boundary against the party, address, message, proofing and consent models and record unresolved overlap as a conflict
Register adopting-Dimension extension codes in a distinct namespace

roles.name: Integration owner
responsibilities: Operate export and import mappings to vCard, JSContact, schema.org and postal templates and document round-trip loss
Keep code-list references synchronized with their governing registries
Ensure inbound values are normalized on ingestion and that ingestion time is recorded separately from event time

roles.name: Access and privacy controller
responsibilities: Define and review the purpose-scoped read rules and masking profiles for endpoint values
Authorize exceptions such as emergency or regulatory disclosure and ensure they are logged in the referenced audit model
Publish the retention schedule and disposition authority applied to contact records

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Contact-point metadata (identifier, endpoint kind, purpose context, validity state) may be read by an actor holding a relationship to the owning party; the endpoint value itself, verification evidence locators and reachability evidence locators require an explicit purpose-scoped grant and are served in the narrowest form that satisfies that purpose.
exceptions: Emergency and life-safety contact use may bypass purpose scoping where the adopting Dimension's policy provides for it; the bypass is recorded with the invoking identity and justification.
Regulatory, judicial or lawful-request disclosure follows the adopting Dimension's legal process, not this model's default rule.
The owning party always has read access to their own contact points, including superseded ones and the verification assertions attached to them.
Public-visibility endpoints marked as publicly readable profiles are exempt from value-level masking but remain subject to purpose scoping for bulk export.
audit_requirements: Every read of a full endpoint value, every verification-status change and every disposition records the actor, the stated purpose, the event instant and the ingestion instant.
Audit records themselves are written to and owned by the referenced audit model; this model stores only the locator and never the audit trail, its retention or its evaluation.
Bulk export and any access exercised under an exception are flagged for review by the access and privacy controller.

read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model by Name and Type and follow Specification URL before assuming any structure
Specification URL - the format-neutral model definition: bundles, layers, findings, data elements, artifacts and boundary notes
Storage type URL - the concrete projection in use (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or other), which is a projection and never the semantics
Interface URL - the access interface in use (MCP, HTTP, file system or other) and its authentication and scoping rules
Processes URL - the registration, normalization, verification-attachment, resolution and supersession procedures and their preconditions
Composition links - resolve referenced party, address, message, proofing and consent models before acting on any element they own

coverage.claim: This structure covers contact-point identity and channel endpoints for WM-PER-010 - stable identity and party binding, endpoint kind/purpose/capability, telephone, email, web/service and postal endpoints, canonical and display forms, internationalization, carried verification assertions, validity, reachability and supersession - grounded in ITU-T, IETF, UPU, W3C, schema.org, SEMIC, OpenID Foundation and NIST sources. Communication preferences and profile governance are declared in scope for the combined model but are delivered by adjacent passes and are not structured here. Lifecycle states, supersession chains and validity intervals are declared as adopting-Dimension extensions because no cited contact standard defines them, and the WM-XCT-024 overlap is unresolved.

checklist.notes: Contact-point identifier separated from endpoint value, with issuing system, scheme and stability questions; identity priority places the master-system identifier first and explicitly bars values and dates. Grounded in JSContact uid/Id keys and vCard UID/PID.

Validity intervals, lifecycle states and supersession are modelled but no cited contact standard defines them: vCard offers only REV and JSContact only created/updated, and CPOV supplies availability rather than record lifecycle. Declared as an adopting-Dimension extension, not as a standards claim.

Owning-party binding, shared and delegated use, role-based holding, postal location reference, evidence locators and the supersession predecessor/successor chain are all modelled as references with explicit ownership boundaries.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated; event time (valid-from/to, supersession effective, assertion instant) is held in elements distinct from observation/ingestion time (record created/updated, verification recorded-at, reachability observed-at).

Value provenance at registration, capability assertion basis (declared/observed/inferred), asserting authority for verification, reachability status setter and transliteration authority are all captured.

Exactly one owning party per contact point, with steward delegation, role-based holding and an accountable owner package. Registry owner (the person or an authorized identity steward) is reflected in the roles and dimension requirements.

Scheme-specific validation is normatively grounded: 15-digit E.164 maximum and CC/NDC/SN structure, mandatory phone-context for local numbers, case-sensitive mailbox local-parts, RFC 3986 comparison ladder, IDNA A-label/U-label convertibility and NFC.

Deny-by-default with purpose-scoped value release, masking, four declared scopes and four exception classes. Enforcement and audit-trail storage are explicitly delegated to the referenced audit model and the adopting Dimension; this model owns only the rule statement.

Soft-disposition, tombstone shape and delegation of erasure execution are specified, but no cited primary source sets retention periods for contact data; the schedule, legal-hold evaluation and data-subject-request workflow are owned by the adopting Dimension and the consent model.

Alignments recorded for E.164/E.123/RFC 3966, RFC 5321/6068/6530/5890, RFC 3986, RFC 9553, RFC 6350, W3C vCard Ontology, schema.org ContactPoint, UPU S42 and CPOV, with the schema.org one-to-many mismatch flagged rather than smoothed over.
NFC, A-label/U-label pairing, UTF-8 mailboxes with no required ASCII fallback, percent-encoded URI carriage, localized variants by locale key and recorded transliteration authority.

Three orthogonal axes separated: medium/scheme, purpose context, and technical capability, each bound to an external code list rather than a local enumeration, with an explicit ambiguity-resolution question.

Assertion carried with authority, method class, assurance level, dual timestamps, expiry and evidence locator; execution, evaluation and audit remain in the referenced proofing model. Grounded in OpenID Connect verified claims and NIST SP 800-63A-4.

Modelled as a derived status plus evidence locator and an ordered acyclic chain, but neither concept is defined by any cited contact standard; the boundary against delivery-attempt logs is asserted by design rather than by an external normative rule.

known_omissions: Communication preferences (preferred channel and rank, preferred language and format, quiet hours, frequency caps, topic scoping) are in scope for the combined WM-PER-010 but are structured in an adjacent pass and appear here only in the model scope statement.

Profile governance beyond the concise service layers - correction and objection handling procedure, stewardship escalation, provenance lineage detail - is delivered by the governance pass, which supplies the canonical service layers.

No accessibility-channel modelling (relay services, textphone routing beyond the vCard textphone capability code, sign-language video relay) is developed, though schema.org contactOption and vCard TYPE hint at it.
Emergency-contact and next-of-kin arrangements, where the contact point reaches a different party than its subject, are only partially covered by the shared-use and care-of elements.
Number portability, carrier reassignment feeds and domain expiry monitoring as triggers for reachability or supersession are referenced conceptually but not modelled.
Device and application endpoints (push tokens, device identifiers) are admitted only via the generic online-service shape; their distinct rotation and revocation semantics are not developed.
ISO 19160-1 could not be retrieved (iso.org returned HTTP 403), so the address conceptual model and its address lifecycle are cited only indirectly through UPU S42.
conflicts: Registry duplication: WM-XCT-024 Contact Point and WM-PER-010 both claim the contact-point concept. The cited vocabularies define one such concept, so the registry must resolve which model owns it; recorded as a conflict and a boundary note rather than a relation.

RFC 5321 requires mailbox local-parts to be treated as case sensitive and their case preserved, while the same RFC notes that exploiting case sensitivity impedes interoperability and is discouraged. Widespread practice lowercases whole addresses. This model follows the normative rule and treats whole-address folding as a defect, which will conflict with many deployed systems.

RFC 6530 removes the requirement for an all-ASCII alternate address for internationalized email, but many downstream systems still demand one. Any recorded ASCII fallback is therefore an optional, separately sourced assertion with a named asserting party, not an equivalence guaranteed by the standard.

schema.org ContactPoint aggregates telephone, email and fax on a single node, whereas JSContact, vCard and this model hold one typed endpoint per object. Export is one-to-many and lossy in round trip; the mismatch is documented rather than resolved by merging.
The W3C vCard Ontology is an Interest Group Note from 2014 and is not a Recommendation; it is used as an RDF alignment only and must not be cited as normative.

No cited standard defines a validity interval, lifecycle state or supersession chain for a contact point. These are the model's most load-bearing extensions and rest on primary support only for the identity separation that makes them possible.

ITU-T E.164 (02/26) is the in-force edition, but the ITU-hosted full text available for verification is the 05/97 edition. The 15-digit maximum and CC/NDC/SN structure are cited from the verified 05/97 text; if the 2026 edition altered them, those specific constraints would need revalidation.
regional_assumptions: E.164 global-number form is assumed available for most telephone endpoints; closed numbering plans, short codes, emergency numbers and PBX extensions require the phone-context mechanism and are treated as local numbers.

Postal delivery assumes UPU member-country templates exist for the country code recorded; informal, descriptive or unaddressed locations common in some regions may have no template and will fall back to captured full text held as provenance only.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 is assumed sufficient for the postal country binding; disputed, non-listed or sub-territorial designations are not resolved by this model.
Internationalized email support is assumed possible but not universal; a given endpoint may be unreachable from ASCII-only infrastructure, which is a reachability fact rather than a validity fact.

Access defaults are stated as deny-by-default with purpose scoping; the specific legal grounds, notification duties and erasure obligations vary by jurisdiction and are deliberately delegated to the adopting Dimension and the consent model.
adversarial_checks: Ownership test against every relation rationale: no bundle, layer, finding or function performs verification, evaluates assurance, executes delivery, enforces access or writes an audit trail. Verification and reachability findings carry assertions and locators only; the delete rules and audit requirements explicitly name the audit model and the adopting Dimension as owners of execution.

Duplication test against the party model: no finding carries a party name, legal identifier, birth data or matching rule. Party binding is a reference tuple with an inline-only rationale stating why no local party artifact exists.

Duplication test against the address model: the postal finding was rejected as an artifact-bearing finding because its structured components belong to UPU S42 templates and the address model; only delivery-role attributes and a reference remain.

Counterexample search on normalization: the attractive but wrong rule 'lowercase the whole email address' was rejected against RFC 5321's MUST on local-part case sensitivity, and the equally attractive 'store the number as typed' was rejected against RFC 3966's separator-insensitive comparison requirement.

Counterexample search on identity: endpoint values were tested as natural keys and rejected, because carriers reassign E.164 numbers and providers recycle mailboxes, so value equality would silently transfer verification assertions between parties.

Unsupported-structure test: every finding was checked for a citation that actually covers its claim. Validity, lifecycle, supersession and reachability failed that test and are marked gaps in the checklist and conflicts rather than presented as standards-backed.

Preference-leakage test: the resolve function was scoped to supersession traversal and canonical dereferencing only, with an explicit effect stating that preference ranking and channel selection belong to the preferences layer, so this pass does not colonize the adjacent split area.
